text: The chain that RWB-E8-015 checks in the target is this service's own local decision-record chain in schema rwb_access, written through the library of DP-03: rwb-access walks the entries it wrote, and the central ledger decision_log_entry and the one central chain over rwb.decision-record.v1 stay with rwb-decision (RWB-P7-E1008-APP, which owns the 02:00 daily check, the verifier and the 15-minute break report). The two controls are complementary and neither is a duplicate: the owner verifies what it wrote, and the ledger verifies the collection.
why: No source names which chain the P4 feature checks. ADR-022 records the decision record as a local record plus a central ledger, ADR-022 and Architecture v5 slide 20 give every service its own decision_record in its own schema, and DP-01 forbids reading decision_log_entry. RWB-P7-E1008-APP already delivers the ledger chain, its verifier and a daily Schedule, so reading the legacy feature as a second central check would duplicate a built story and break DP-01. The owner-side reading is the only one that is both consistent with DP-01 and already specified for P7.

text: The chain check is served by two operations fixed on the DP-13 base of rwb-access: POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/chain-checks, which has no body, takes a required Idempotency-Key and answers the run row with 201, and GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/chain-checks, which takes the outcome filter and the page bounds and answers the report page. Neither is an ownership-map row, both are declared as provided by RWB-P4-E8015-CON, and no other story owns them.
why: The legacy story names only the rule-version paths, the FSD gives the feature no interface, the TSD gives it no endpoint and the ownership map gives rwb-access four unrelated operations. An app story cannot be built and a route cannot be composed without a path, so the paths are fixed on the service base of DP-13 and the point is carried as CG-B2-P4-015-1 instead of being left blank in the metadata.

text: The run row of a chain check carries checkId, outcome (a closed set of CLEAN and BROKEN), entriesChecked, verifiedThrough, firstBrokenEntryId (present only on a breach), windowFrom, windowTo, trigger (SCHEDULED or ON_DEMAND), checkedAt and entryId; the report page carries items, checkpointEntryId, page, size and total. The record of a run is one append to the local decision-record chain, the checkpoint is a row of this service moved only by a CLEAN run, and the report is a projection over the entries that carry the library's chain-check record code, so no new table is introduced.
why: No source lists the fields of a chain-check result and the ownership map has no table for run rows. A new table would need a DB slice that this Work Package does not carry and would put the record of a control outside the append-only chain that the control exists to protect. The DP-03 library already publishes an entry with a code, an inputs reference, a time and the two hashes, which is enough to hold a run and to answer it.

text: The cadence of the daily check is the one REQ-DRI-003 and NFR-035 fix (daily, with the break reported the same business day) and it is held as a parameter row read through DP-06 with the version in force; the start time of the Schedule, the order and batch size of the walk, the window and the page bounds are parameter rows as well, the record code of a chain check is the DP-03 library's, and no interval, batch size or page bound is a constant in code. The same-day report to Compliance and internal audit is the recorded breach row plus the report read; a notice through rwb-comms is out of scope of this Work Package because it is not in the dependency lists.
why: REQ-DRI-003 and NFR-035 fix the cadence and the same-day obligation and fix nothing else; BR-P4-026 and DP-06 require every value a business person may change to be reference data with a version rather than code; and no source names a notification channel for this feature, so inventing one would add a contract dependency the Work Package does not carry.

text: Both chain-check operations authorise Platform administration R, which RW-AUDIT, RW-COMPLY, RW-PLATADM, RW-SECADM, RW-DATASTEW and RW-COE hold in the TSD P4 v3 T6.1 matrix: internal audit reads the runs and the breaches and may start an on-demand run, and a case role with a dash in Platform administration is refused with 403 and MSG-P4-002. The legacy permission checks of Rules and parameters C for RW-COE and A for RW-RISK are not applied, because they belong to the rule-version feature of RWB-E8-007 and not to a read-only walk.
why: The FSD role table says the feature runs unattended with internal audit as the second user, the TSD matrix gives RW-AUDIT R in Platform administration and RW-RISK no administration letter at all, and the legacy C and A letters describe an upload and an approval that a chain check does not have. Applying the legacy letters would refuse the only role the FSD names as a user.

text: A break is reported on the same business day by the recorded breach row and by the report read: the run row with outcome BROKEN, its firstBrokenEntryId and its verifiedThrough is available on SCR-43 Roles and access and on GET /admin/chain-checks as soon as the run commits, and the Compliance and PDPA officer role and internal audit read it there. The checkpoint does not move on a BROKEN run, so every later run re-raises the same break until the chain verifies again, and no entry is repaired by this service.
why: REQ-DRI-003 and NFR-035 require a same-day report and name no channel and no recipient beyond Compliance; the report read is the only channel this Work Package carries a dependency for, and the re-raise makes the finding durable without a second store.

text: The daily run is the Schedule chain-check-daily on the queue rwb-access and the workflow AccessChainCheckWorkflow with the activities readCheckWindow, recomputeChainRange and recordCheckResult, built against the platform workflow kit and its Schedule API (RWB-PLT-WF, RWB-PLT-E1071-CON) although that contract story is not in this Work Package's H list. The metadata is kept exactly as the Work Package fixes it and the missing H is stated in the story, in section 13 and in CG-B2-P4-015-4.
why: An unattended daily check cannot be built without the Schedule API, and DP-10 makes the workflow kit a platform contract dependency of any story that schedules work. The Work Package lists four H dependencies and none of them is the kit, so the story cannot both honour the metadata and hide the prerequisite; it keeps the metadata and records the omission.
